import { LinkCard, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import OssMarquee from '../../components/OssMarquee.astro';

<div class="pz-section">
## A pipeline is a file in your repo.

Whether you write it yourself or an agent drafts it, it ends up in the
same place — SQL and YAML you can read, diff, and review like anything
else your team ships.

<div class="pz-cols">

```sql title="pipelines/orders_enriched.sql"
INSERT INTO {{ sink('lake', 'orders_curated',
    strategy: 'replace', format: 'parquet') }}
SELECT
    o.id,
    o.amount,
    c.email
FROM {{ ref('stg_orders') }} AS o
JOIN {{ source('raw', 'customers') }} AS c
    ON c.id = o.customer_id
```

```yaml title="connections.yml"
raw:
  connector: localfiles
  entities:
    customers:
      read:
        path: data/customers.csv
        format: csv

lake:
  connector: localfiles
  root: out   # writes land under out/<entity>/
```

</div>

<div class="pz-pr-row">
<div class="pz-pr-copy">
### Change it, and someone reads the diff.

No config UI holds the logic hostage — a bad join or a silent strategy
change gets caught in review, not in production.
</div>

<div class="pz-diff">
<div class="pz-diff-head">
<span class="fname">pipelines/orders_enriched.sql</span>
<span class="stat"><span class="add">+3</span> <span class="rem">-1</span></span>
</div>
<pre><span class="dl ctx"> INSERT INTO {'{'}{'{'} sink('lake', 'orders_curated',</span><span class="dl rem"><span class="mark-rem">-</span>    strategy: 'replace', format: 'parquet') {'}'}{'}'}</span><span class="dl add"><span class="mark">+</span>    strategy: 'merge', key: ['id'], format: 'parquet') {'}'}{'}'}</span><span class="dl ctx"> SELECT</span><span class="dl ctx">     o.id,</span><span class="dl ctx">     o.amount,</span><span class="dl ctx">     c.email</span><span class="dl ctx"> FROM {'{'}{'{'} ref('stg_orders') {'}'}{'}'} AS o</span><span class="dl ctx"> JOIN {'{'}{'{'} source('raw', 'customers') {'}'}{'}'} AS c</span><span class="dl ctx">     ON c.id = o.customer_id</span><span class="dl add"><span class="mark">+</span>WHERE o.amount &gt; 0</span></pre>
<div class="pz-review">
<span class="pz-avatar">MR</span>
<div class="pz-review-body">
LGTM — <code>replace</code> was silently dropping late updates.
<div class="pz-review-chip">✓ pz validate — 2 checks passed</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="pz-section">
## Ingestion, spoken into existence.

Describe the pipeline. An MCP-connected agent writes valid SQL, `pz`
verifies every edit, and it's running before you've finished your coffee.

<div class="pz-demo">
<div class="pz-prompt">
<div>
<div class="pz-bubble-tag">You</div>
<div class="pz-bubble pz-bubble-you">Add a pipeline for total order value per customer, merged into postgres.</div>
</div>
<div>
<div class="pz-bubble-tag">pz agent · via MCP</div>
<div class="pz-bubble">Drafting <code>customer_order_summary.sql</code>, validating against the current DAG…</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="pz-term">
<div class="pz-term-bar"><i></i><i></i><i></i><span>pz mcp — customer_order_summary.sql</span></div>
<div class="pz-term-zone">
<div class="file-tag">pipelines/customer_order_summary.sql</div>
<pre><span class="kw">insert into</span> {'{'}{'{'} <span class="fn">sink</span>('postgres', 'customer_order_summary', strategy: 'merge', key: ['customer_id']) {'}'}{'}'}
<span class="kw">select</span>
    c.id <span class="kw">as</span> customer_id,
    count(o.id) <span class="kw">as</span> order_count,
    sum(o.amount) <span class="kw">as</span> total_amount
<span class="kw">from</span> {'{'}{'{'} <span class="fn">ref</span>('stg_orders') {'}'}{'}'} <span class="kw">as</span> o
<span class="kw">join</span> {'{'}{'{'} <span class="fn">source</span>('raw', 'customers') {'}'}{'}'} <span class="kw">as</span> c
    <span class="kw">on</span> c.id = o.customer_id
<span class="kw">group by</span> c.id;</pre>
</div>
<div class="pz-term-zone">
<pre><span class="dim">$</span> pz validate
<span class="ok">ok</span>  customer_order_summary  schema resolved, 2 upstreams
<span class="dim">$</span> pz run --all
<span class="ok">ok</span>  customer_order_summary  <span class="dim">3 rows 18ms</span></pre>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="pz-section">
## Running in five minutes

<Steps>

1. Install the CLI as a .NET global tool:

   ```console
   $ dotnet tool install --global pz
   ```

2. Scaffold a small, complete, runnable project:

   ```console
   $ pz init demo --template sample && cd demo
   ```

   (Bare `pz init` scaffolds the minimal template instead — the right start for your own
   data. `--template sample` is what ships the bundled CSVs this walkthrough runs;
   `pz init --list-templates` shows all five.)

3. Run both flows — sources, pipelines, checks, and sinks in one command:

   ```console
   $ pz run --all
   ```

</Steps>
</div>
